items.reviewNote: Avez cru and qui avez donné are compound-tense auxiliary uses; the God vocative uses honorific second-plural vous agreement. The existing avez possession bank was inspected and remains unchanged. Attach this surface to the already distinct published avoir auxiliary sense, without copying possession mastery or inventing a tense-only meaning. All three complete questions test auxiliary function; the middle four options can each precede a past participle, and passé composé selects the present auxiliary.

Qu’auraient-ils à dire asks what content the creatures would have available to say. The published qu’aurait bank is explicitly compound-tense auxiliary, qu’as asks about illness or possession, and the earlier qu’ai à faire de bank tests relationship; all were inspected and excluded as question banks. The global lexical avoir sense explicitly covers abstract as well as concrete possession, so this surface targets that existing sense under lem_avoir. The fused spelling does not create a tense-only sense or another lemma; que stays inside the exact token, and final import must not duplicate an interrogative component encounter. All middle prefixes form grammatical plural hypothetical questions, distinguished by have/buy/lose/make semantics. No earlier mastery is copied.

The dwarf asks how the tiny beings could have vocal organs. The existing how sense and all three published banks were inspected; their answer capitalization Comment does not match this source’s interior lowercase surface. Add a lowercase contextual bank on the same meaning, rather than inventing a case-only sense or mutating the earlier sentence-initial bank. All four middle question adverbs are grammatical, while manner rather than time, location or cause selects comment; final surface normalization must preserve existing how mastery.

Sans en être entendue means without the voice being heard by the mites. The proper published French en pronoun sense already reprises a de complement, independently of the preposition or gerund lemmas. OQLF supports en referring to a de complement including an animal/person, and supports de as a passive-participle complement introducer; the precise historical agent reading in this sentence is an explicit contextual inference from voix and mites, not a verbatim quotation from those pages. Add this contextual bank on the existing de-reference sense, without creating an agent-only duplicate or copying mastery from prepositional en. The middle question names the source pronoun so alternatives remain grammatical labels and the reference role selects en.

The four pour occurrences at unit 167 relate scales: small animals to bees, bees to humankind, the Sirian to vast animals, and those vast animals to still larger substances. The global published pour has only beneficiary/purpose questions and the earlier pour moi bank marks personal viewpoint; neither tests this relational analogy. Prepare relational correspondence under the existing French preposition lemma, without a new comparison-only lemma. All alternatives fit the grammatical prepositional slot; correspondence rather than opposition, absence or location selects pour. No published bank is changed; final reconciliation must compare this proposed relation sense with every other workwide pour context before import.

manualReviewNotes: The four new banks were inspected in all three bands; the earlier avez bank was re-read and inherited unchanged. This exact bank ledger includes 12 new bands and three retained bands, with no noun questions in these five banks.

Qu’auraient tests lexical abstract availability; comment tests manner without a case-only sense; passive-agent en reprises the mites under the proper pronoun sense; pour tests relational analogy under the existing preposition lemma. All middle alternatives fit their unchanged stems.
